originalTitle: More than 16 killed as Kyiv comes under intense Russian bombardment
summary: Missile and drone attack one of heaviest since war began, with children’s hospital and residential areas hit
content: A heavy Russian missile and drone bombardment has killed at least 16 people in and around Kyiv in one of the most intense aerial attacks on Ukraine’s capital since the start of the war. Vitali Klitschko, the city’s mayor, said homes, a school and a children’s medical centre were among the buildings damaged overnight in an attack that began at about midnight and was continuing into the early afternoon. Sixteen people were reported killed in the city, officials said, while other authorities said 33 had been injured. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said: “It was a massive attack – the Russians had been preparing for a long time, combining different types of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones, aiming to cause as much damage as possible to civilian infrastructure.” Explosions could be clearly heard from the city centre within minutes of the first warning at 11.51pm on Wednesday, earlier than the normal timing of Russian missile strikes. A further wave of attacks followed after 6am on Thursday, and drone threats continued throughout the morning. Ukraine’s air force said Russia had launched dozens of ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles and 168 drones in the overnight attack. Later it reported shooting down 41 out of 46 cruise missiles and 145 drones, although none of an unspecified number of high-speed ballistic missiles was intercepted. A shortage of Patriot interceptors means that Ukraine is struggling to defend itself from attack from high-speed ballistics, which can arrive within minutes of an air raid warning. Earlier this month, the air force decided to stop announcing how many ballistics had been launched, citing security concerns. Eight people were reported killed in the Solomianskyi district to the west of the centre of the capital. A multistorey apartment building in a residential area was struck and flats on the top floor destroyed, killing two, rescuers said. An empty building, sometimes used informally as a shelter, in the middle of a car park was destroyed in a strike at about midnight. Nobody was reported killed, though several cars were burnt out and bricks from the building scattered several metres across the open space nearby. Oleksandr, a car park attendant, was on duty at the time of the attack and escaped with light injuries. The next morning, still shocked, covered in cuts, his shorts torn into strips, he waited by his destroyed booth and said he could not remember what had happened to him immediately after the blast. Andriy, 57, a driver, said he first heard an explosion close by and was in his vehicle when the strike on the building in the car park took place. He said he believed his life was saved by the tinted plastic sheeting he had stuck on to his car windows. “I was only scratched on the back of my head,” he added. There was no sign of any military or industrial activity in the local area. The car park was used by residents of the nearby apartment blocks, and the non-residential buildings largely disused. Zelenskyy urged a global response to the attacks. “While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy said on social media. An attack in Brovary district in the wider Kyiv region killed one man and wounded another, said the regional governor, Tymur Tkachenko. “One industrial facility has been damaged. All relevant services are on site, working to extinguish the fire,” he said. Warehouses in Boryspil, east of Kyiv, were also attacked, including a facility operated by the Ukrainian Red Cross, Ukraine’s prime minister, Sergiy Koretsky, said. Both sides have been escalating long-range attacks while air defences remain short. Ukraine has attacked oil refineries and warehouses close to Moscow using newly developed cruise missiles and drones, while Russia has stepped up its attacks on Kyiv, making heavy use of hard ballistics. The Ukrainian air force said Kinzhal and Zircon hypersonic missiles were used in the attack, as well as Iskander and North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles, sea-launched Kalibr cruise missiles and Shahed drones. Ukraine’s air force had earlier warned of Russian Kalibr missiles passing over the regional village of Kaharlyk and heading towards the capital. Eight of the missiles had been launched from warships in the Black Sea, though all were shot down. Romania’s defence ministry said radar systems detected aerial targets near the Ukrainian border overnight, prompting the scrambling of two Spanish fighter jets deployed on Nato missions and a Romanian air force helicopter. The ministry said a drone entered Romanian airspace near Galați before crashing in an unpopulated area in Tulcea county. Poland’s military command said it had mobilised aircraft and activated air defences aimed at protecting Polish airspace, particularly in areas bordering Ukraine. Finland’s defence ministry said on Thursday evening that it suspected a Russian aircraft had violated its airspace earlier in the day. Russia also reported a large Ukrainian drone attack. Moscow’s mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, said 250 drones had flown toward the Moscow region between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, and that most had been destroyed at a significant distance from the capital itself. Moscow confirmed on Wednesday that Russia was having to import refined petroleum products to try to stabilise supply following Ukraine’s attacks on its refineries. The Reuters news agency used industry contacts and market data to establish that a tanker from India had recently arrived and unloaded, while supplies were also being sourced from east Asia.
chineseTitle: 基辅遭到俄罗斯猛烈轰炸，造成超过 16 人死亡
chineseSummary: 导弹和​​无人机袭击是战争开始以来最严重的袭击之一，儿童医院和居民区遭到袭击
chineseContent: 俄罗斯导弹和无人机的猛烈轰炸已造成基辅及其周边地区至少 16 人死亡，这是自战争开始以来对乌克兰首都最猛烈的空袭之一。该市市长维塔利·克里琴科表示，袭击从午夜左右开始，一直持续到下午早些时候，连夜受损的建筑包括房屋、学校和儿童医疗中心。官员称，据报道该市有 16 人死亡，其他当局称 33 人受伤。乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基表示：“这是一次大规模袭击——俄罗斯人已经准备了很长时间，结合了不同类型的弹道导弹、巡航导弹和无人机，旨在对民用基础设施造成尽可能多的破坏。”周三晚上 11 点 51 分，在首次发出警报后几分钟内，市中心就可以清楚地听到爆炸声，这比俄罗斯导弹袭击的正常时间要早。周四早上 6 点之后又发生了一波袭击，无人机威胁整个上午都在持续。乌克兰空军表示，俄罗斯在夜间袭击中发射了数十枚弹道导弹、巡航导弹和高超音速导弹以及 168 架无人机。后来它报告击落了 46 枚巡航导弹中的 41 枚和 145 架无人机，但没有拦截任何数量不详的高速弹道导弹。爱国者拦截机的短缺意味着乌克兰正在努力防御高速弹道导弹的攻击，而高速弹道导弹可能会在空袭警报发出后几分钟内到达。本月早些时候，空军以安全考虑为由，决定停止公布发射了多少弹道导弹。据报道，首都市中心以西的索洛米扬斯基区有八人死亡。是
